steps.text: Preheat an oven to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C). Coat 2 baking sheets with nonstick cooking spray.

Combine brown sugar, pumpkin pie spice, rolled oats, almonds, and pecans in a large bowl. Mix the applesauce, honey, and vanilla in a separate large bowl. Stir the oat mixture into the applesauce mixture, until granola begins to gather in clusters. Spoon granola evenly onto prepared baking sheets.
Bake in preheated oven, stirring every 20 minutes, until lightly browned and crispy, about 1 hour.
Remove from oven; cool to room temperature. Stir in raisins and cranberries; store in an airtight container.

raw_recipe.headline: Crunchy Pumpkin Pie Granola
raw_recipe.description: A big bowl of granola is a great way to start your day. In this crunchy version, sweetened rolled oats and nuts are mixed with pumpkin pie spice, baked until crispy, and tossed with dried fruit.
raw_recipe.name: Crunchy Pumpkin Pie Granola

review.reviewBody: I actually ended up changing this recipe a bit. I didn't have the proper pumpkin spice mix so I just added cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg. Didn't have pecans, so I used almonds. To make it more like pumpkin pie I used pumpkin puree instead of apple sauce. Found I had to bake it longer than the recipe showed, but it continued to dry after I removed it from the oven. It has excellent pumpkin flavour with the puree in there and the whole family loved it. Will definitely make this time and time again! Don't be afraid to play around with the recipe.

Wonderful granola! I used 5 grain plus flaxseed whole grain cereal (Bob's Red Mill) & added dried apples and used walnuts instead of pecans. I also turned the oven up to 300 degrees the last 20 minutes.

Will make it again! Added 1/2 cup of wheat bran. Substituted raw pumpkin seeds for the raisins. Having made my own granola for years I know that adding dried fruit to your granola while it's in the storage container will cause it to lose it's crunch, but nuts and seeds are fine. Did need to increase the baking time. Next time I will experiment with increasing the oven temperature.

Update 2019 review: I have now made many batches of granola using other recipes and decided to revisit this one and tweak it a bit. It's not crunchy because the applesauce replaces the oil that is normally there; so I used 1/2 cup applesauce and 1/4 cup oil and got the crunchy texture I wanted. I also added 1/2 tsp salt to bring out more flavor. 
Those changes did it for me! I also, because of what I had on hand, substituted pumpkin seeds for the slivered almonds and dried sweet cherries for the raisins/cranberries, and these both worked great.

Original 2015 review: I followed the recipe exactly, and yeah, there's not a lot of pumpkin flavor. It probably would be better to substitute pumpkin puree for the applesauce. Also I didn't love the texture; my regular granola is made with maple syrup, and that gets much crunchier than this granola did. It probably would be better over yogurt as one reviewer suggested, but I don't find it very satisfying as a standalone breakfast. It did smell amazing in the oven!

I made this recipe using Libby's Pumpkin Pie Mix - the sweetened stuff. By decreasing the honey slightly, it made for a great substitution for the applesauce and REALLY amped up the pumpkin theme. This is some great granola, yum!

I have been trying different recipes for this Thanksgiving feast and this recipe is awesome but instead of using pumpkin purée I used sweet tators (cooked them like I was making a pie) using allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, etc and no applesauce. Added 1 tsp of sweet chili powder and toasted my pecans, almonds and walnuts. Stirred and cooked accordingly. Then I drizzled more honey on top of mixture and made into small bite size balls. You can play around with this recipe and no one person would ever be disappointed. Thanks for the recipe

This was my first granola making experience, and I'm quite proud of the results! I didn't have applesauce on hand and using it over oil was the primary reason I used this recipe. I pureed apples in the blender instead and it worked perfectly. I also used agave instead of honey and baked it at 275. It doesn't really taste like pumpkin pie, but it's delicious, nonetheless! I left out the fruits so I can add whatever I feel like the day I'm eating it. Great recipe!

I made this yesterday. Instead of baking in the oven, I cooked it in my crock pot (which I've also done with another granola recipe). I used a crock pot bag and a vented lid from one of my regular pots instead of the glass crock pot lid. I let it cook on high for 2-3 hours, turned it down to low, removed the lid, and let it cook for probably another hour. I stirred it a couple times during the cooking process. It did have a crunchiness to it even though I made it in the crock pot. I added the craisins and raisins after it was done cooking per the directions. Flavor-wise I wasn't wowed. I have a cherry almond granola recipe (Light and Tasty magazine; here's the link for anyone interested http://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/cherry-almond-granola) that I like better so I probably won't make this particular recipe again.

I took larkspur's tip and used Trader Joe's pumpkin puree instead of applesauce. I did not use dried cranberries because I do not have any. This was so simple to make and it turned out fantastic! All three of us (my two sons and myself) thought this was one of the best granolas we've ever had. I made this early this morning and let it cool and we had it for breakfast an hour later so it was nice and fresh and crunchy. I have about a cup leftover that I stuck in Tupperware, I'll update my review if it turns out that it's less not as good the next day. I don't think of pumpkin pie when I eat it but it does make me think of fall/winter. I'll make this again--next time I'll try this with applesauce and my homemade apple pie spice.

It took all of my power to to rate this while I was cooking it. It made my apartment smell sooooo GOOD!! Smell aside, this is a terrific granola recipe. This is the first time I've made granola, so after browsing through all the other recipes I decided to try for this one, since it didn't use oil. SO happy I did! I read the other reviews and decided to compromise with the oven at 275. It took a little longer to cook, 1 hour 15 minutes, but after letting it sit, it became much more crunchy and I decided I may have overcooked it very slightly. I also used walnuts instead of pecans because that's what I had on hand. Added a few dashes of cinnamon as well. Other than that stayed true to the recipe, and so glad I did. While it didn't really taste much like pumpkin pie, the flavors worked so well together, it didn't seem to matter! No more expensive store bought granola for me!

This is an incredibly flavorful granola. The blend of pumpkin pie spice and applesauce is an incredibly beautiful balance. I cooked it about 30 minutes more than the recipe said to get it crispy. The perfect fall granola!

I wanted to love this recipe. I grow pumpkins, my family LOVES pumpkin bread. It looked economical and healthy, but alas, it turned out chewy, not very sweet and my kids declared it a fail. I choked some down with milk. The family declared it unfit to top their yogurt (because chewy). I made it two months ago and I still have left overs in a jar. Now you may be different. You may want to decrease fats in your life and try to use alternatives. For you this might work, but if you love the taste of butter, or coconut oil or any conventional oil for that matter, the sheer lack of oil in this recipe is going to be noticeable. Your oats are not going to have that toasted flavor you associate with granola. Just know that going in. Is it edible? Yes. Is it remotely like any granola you have tried? No. I've got to be honest. It's not.
This recipe is amazing!!! My family loves it!!! Healthy, tasty, and absolutely perfect everytime. Thank you!!! So delicious!!!
Delicious and so easy. This recipe is easy to change up. I used walnuts in place of pecans because I did not have the latter.
Sounds great, however, does anyone have any idea how to change it to make it half way healthy for diabetics?

Lots of pumpkin pie spice flavour.
I used pumpkin seeds because that's what I had and they were good. A little sweeter than I like. I'd definetly make again but reduce sugar.

I love this! So delicious and super easy to make. As others have suggested, I used puréed pumpkin in place of the applesauce (with excellent results). I also added pepitas and roasted, unsalted sunflower seeds as well as the pecans and almonds. Everything in this is healthy, so you can feel good about indulging. Paired with yogurt, it's a real treat! Thank you for this great recipe.
I only used almonds. Didn't put honey in it, as a friend is deathly allergic to it, only used brown sugar. I am a granola and pumpkin spice fan - the two together? What can go wrong! Very tasty!!

Hubby made & thinks it is a 5, I would say a 4. It is very filling so can't eat much at a time. Hubby says this is the best granola recipe we have & I do agree. Will make again. Didn't change a thing, but may add a little more cranberries just because we love them.

I used canned pumpkin in place of applesauce, and the pumpkin adds a fruity note just as I would expect from applesauce. You won't notice that there is no butter or oil in this recipe--it's crunchy and just what a granola should be.
